DO NOT TRIGGER WHEN: the concern is runtime flow with no initialization phase (use distributed-flow-auditor).

Application-hygiene auditor for dead code, orphan assets, unused dependencies, stale docs and migration/debug leftovers. TRIGGER WHEN: dispatched by senior-reviews review method under /daodan:review-changes or /daodan:review-branch, by /daodan:tidy-repo or /daodan:check-health, or asked for a technical-debt, dead-code, orphan-asset or unused-dependency audit. DO NOT TRIGGER WHEN: applying removals (use senior-review:application-cleanup-method under commit authorization, from /daodan:tidy-repo), filesystem/git tidying (use repo-hygiene:workspace-auditor), or single-language scans (use typescript-development:knip or python-development:python-dead-code).

Hunts coupling violations, broken abstractions, resource leaks, stale caches, and anti-patterns. TRIGGER WHEN: the user asks for a code review, architecture audit, quality scoring, failure-path analysis, or pattern consistency check. DO NOT TRIGGER WHEN: the task is security-specific auditing (use security-auditor).

Persistence-layer reviewer for partial writes, read-modify-write races, missing DB uniqueness constraints and cache-database divergence. TRIGGER WHEN: target touches schemas, models, ORM entities, repositories, raw SQL, caches or transaction boundaries. DO NOT TRIGGER WHEN: domain rules/state machines (use logic-integrity-auditor) or cross-service message flows (use distributed-flow-auditor).

Hunts cascading timeout violations, missing idempotency, broken saga compensation, message ordering bugs, and split-brain risks. TRIGGER WHEN: the target spans microservices, agent systems, or multiple modules and the question is cross-service: request flow tracing, contract mismatch between producer and consumer, or integration-boundary review.

Cross-component reviewer for ordering, idempotency, state machines, terminal states and domain invariants in .team-review/02-interconnect.md, or in a scoped semantic context when no interconnect map exists. TRIGGER WHEN: Phase 2 of senior-reviews branch review (/daodan:review-branch) runs, a lite review supplies a scoped semantic context, or asked for a logic, contract or invariant audit. DO NOT TRIGGER WHEN: style/lint review (use code-auditor), security-only review (use security-auditor), or neither an interconnect map nor a scoped semantic context is supplied (report the missing prerequisite; in team review, semantic-interconnect-mapper can build the map).

Derives independent code claims (Mode 1, blind to shared maps), challenges load-bearing finding premises (Mode 2, Lens 0) and checks what a plan, record or document claims about the code (Mode 3). TRIGGER WHEN: Phase 1c of senior-reviews branch review (/daodan:review-branch) runs, the verification panel spawns Lens 0 for a finding premise, or a review of a plan, a specification or a document dispatches the claim check. DO NOT TRIGGER WHEN: hunting defects (use dimension auditors) or building the interconnect map (use codebase-map:semantic-interconnect-mapper).

Reviewer for resource acquisition and release across success, error and cancellation paths: leaks, double-release, use-after-release and unbounded pools. TRIGGER WHEN: target acquires file handles, sockets, streams, DB connections, subprocesses, listeners, locks, threads, timers or GPU/native memory. DO NOT TRIGGER WHEN: behavior over time after a leak (use temporal-resilience-auditor), memory-safety exploitation (use security-auditor), or general architecture (use code-auditor).

Attacker-mindset pass over the target: assumes it is exploitable and proves it. TRIGGER WHEN: the user asks for a security review, SAST audit, OWASP or CWE analysis, secret-leak scan, or an authentication or authorization code review; injection vectors, auth bypasses, crypto mistakes, or missing security headers; the target exposes URLs, routes or functions to untrusted callers; code reads or returns data by a caller-supplied ID (IDOR / data theft); code checks permissions, roles or ownership; or code creates, verifies or destroys logins and sessions. DO NOT TRIGGER WHEN: the concern is general code quality (use code-auditor) or infrastructure and network security (use platform-reviewer).

Reviewer for failure-over-time defects: missing backoff/caps, silent subsystem death, uncleared guards, notification floods and clock hazards. TRIGGER WHEN: reviewing timers, schedulers, polling loops, retry/reconnect logic, queues, cron jobs, background workers or watchdogs. DO NOT TRIGGER WHEN: startup/bootstrap cycles (use chicken-egg-detector), cross-service timeout chains (use distributed-flow-auditor), or UI rendering races (use ui-race-auditor).

Framework-agnostic UI timing analyst: React, Angular, Vue, Qt, GTK, Flutter, SwiftUI, Electron, Tauri. TRIGGER WHEN: races between async data loading, layout, event handlers, and programmatic scroll, focus, or resize; scroll position corruption, sticky or auto-scroll breakage, focus theft, layout shift, stale measurement closures, layout-dependent reads racing incomplete renders.
